Hi <!here>,
Have you been able to make a clear decision about our ideas? What direction should we take with the scenario?
Do you have any suggestions in addition to the scenarios we've prepared?
Hi, the entire product team is out today (in Turkey we observe the Aug 30th and in the US we have a long weekend). We’ll circle back with you over the next day or two. Thank you for the follow up!
hey guys, sorry we are silent - some product work took priority - we’ll circle back with you as soon as we can

Hi <@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID>, the way I see it, playables can be good for optimizing for CPIs (fun casual playable but unrelated to core game), optimizing for retention (filter out users that are not going to like your game), or somewhere in the middle. I think Scenario 1 is a good bet for filtering out the players that won't like our game, while remaining true to our core game play.

For Scenario 1, would the user be able to select any items they want and make several matches (if they are good enough)? I like that idea -- but will call out it seems a lot more sophisticated than the Domino Delights playable where the user is essentially on rails and only makes a few matches before the playable ends.

Hi <@EMPLOYEE_0008_SLACK_ID>,
Thanks for your feedback and thoughts! I agree with your perspective on Scenario 1 being a good way to filter players who might not enjoy the game while staying true to our core gameplay.
Regarding your question: yes, the idea is that the user can select items freely and make multiple matches if they are skilled enough.

<@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID> lets go with Scenario 1. From a design standpoint, I think the main elements to figure out are 1) what items are on the board, and 2) what zombies are being smashed.

For items, we want to highlight that different items have different abilities and choose items that might be especially entertaining to the users. I think grenade (powerful), couch (splash damage), plush doll (weak but potentially funny), would be a good start.

For zombies, we have quite a few at this point. Probably best to use a variety.

What are next steps for us to Push this project forward?

Hello <@EMPLOYEE_0008_SLACK_ID>,
We are planning to start this project on *September 29*. If you can share the assets with us before that date, we’ll be able to start the optimization and animation processes in advance.
For the items on the board, we can make them editable. This way, aside from the 8-item set that you will provide for the board, you can also test any additional items you’d like to try in the game.
 For the zombies, we will proceed with animations in Spine. You can select which zombies from the platform you’d like to use in the game. Depending on the overall game size, we can finalize the number of zombies during the project.
Here are the asset formats we can work with:
• *3D assets*: .fbx, .glb, or .blend (when exporting .fbx, please make sure it’s exported in *Binary format*, not ASCII)
• *2D assets*: .png (for 2D animations, character parts need to be separated into pieces)
• *Font*: .ttf or .woff2
• *Sound*: .mp3 or .wav
hi <@EMPLOYEE_0008_SLACK_ID> Do you have an idea of when you’ll be able to share the assets with us?

<@EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID> can you help package up assets? <@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID> can you help [PERSON_NAME_0092] narrow down what is needed? Any examples you could share of specifically what you're after would be helpful.

Hello <@EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID>*,*
Here is the list of assets we are expecting from your side:
*3D Assets:* Zombie models + animations, rocket launcher, projectile, board items (the specific objects you’d like to be used on the board)
 *2D Assets:* Item visuals, UI elements, background
 *Audio:* Matching sound, rocket sound, explosion sound, success/failure sounds, background music
 *Text:* Fonts
*Formats:*
• 3D assets: .fbx, .glb, or .blend (when exporting .fbx, please make sure it’s exported in *Binary* format, not ASCII)
• 2D assets: .png (for 2D animations, character parts need to be separated into pieces)
• Font: .ttf or .woff2
• Sound: .mp3 or .wav
Regarding the board assets, depending on the project size, we can provide a system where you can directly upload and test the assets on the board yourself.

We shared a platform screenshot of a previously completed game with a similar mechanic as an example. In that project, we embedded the assets they provided directly into the game. Additionally, we added a system where they could upload assets to the platform themselves. From There, they could select and use the assets however they wanted.

Hi <@EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID>,
 When will you be able to share the assets? Before starting the project, we’ll need to optimize them and check if anything is missing.

Hello  <@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID>,
Sorry for the late reply. I will send all the assets by Wednesday at the latest. First, we need to finalize which items and zombies will be used on the Design side. After that, I will gather the assets and zip them
<@EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID> Thank you so much, looking forward to receiving the assets!

Hi <@EMPLOYEE_0008_SLACK_ID>, We wanted to let you know that due to a delay in receiving the assets, we need to update the project start date. Normally, before starting we optimize and review the assets to make sure everything runs smoothly. Because of this, we’ll be able to kick off your project on *October 6th*.

Hi <@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID>!  You can access the game assets here. Since our zombies are made with 2D Unity animations, I’ve included the PSD files along with the animation and prefab files. Please let me know if you find any missing or problematic assets
We’ve also prepared a sample level as a reference. The fail condition in the game is when zombies reach us and deplete our HP, while the win condition is eliminating all the zombies on screen

Additionally as you mentioned, we’re planning to add different items and zombie types later on for testing. Also, having control over the number of zombies and items placed on the board will give us a lot of flexibility

*Hi <@EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID>,*
Thank you for sharing the assets. We’ll review them and get back to you if we notice any missing elements.
At this stage, the only missing piece seems to be the duck asset used in the reference. Could you also provide that? In addition, it would be great if you could share the zombie assets in *Unity package* format along with their animations.
We’ll be re-animating the selected zombies in Spine and integrating them into the project that way. If There are no size limitations, we can also upload the zombies to the platform in a way that allows you to select and use them directly. As for the upload compatibility, we’ll clarify this later in the project and keep you updated.
<@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID> Sure, I’m sending the files. Thanks for the update
<@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID> noted on revised kick off time.

Hi <@EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID>,
We’ve checked the zombie assets, but it looks like the package wasn’t exported correctly. Only the prefabs were included, but the actual assets are missing. In order to view the prefabs properly, we also need all the related .png files to be part of the package. Right now, when we import it into Unity, we only see the prefabs, which are not usable without the assets.
Could you please make sure all the necessary files are selected during export? To avoid any extra issues, it would be great if you could test the package in a blank Unity project before sending it over.
<@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID> Sorry, it took a little while, I had to get help from our animator
<@EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID> Thank you. We’ll review the assets and let you know if we encounter any issues.

<@EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID> hi again :[USERNAME_42310]:

We have reviewed the assets. Since we don’t use Unity to develop the playables, we need to adapt the characters you provided to our pipeline. To do this, we will re-rig the characters in Spine and extract the keyframes from the Unity animations via script to recreate the same animations in Spine.
However, the characters you sent currently have a large number of animations, and transferring all of them individually would be very time-consuming.
To proceed more efficiently, we kindly ask you to:
• Select the primary animation you want us to use (attack, idle, die, or walk), and
• Specify the 4 zombie characters to which this animation should be applied.
Depending on the project scope and size, we can increase the number of zombies in later stages. For now, 4 characters seem to be the most suitable option in terms of both time and size.

<@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID> we are considering a pretty substantial pivot in core game play for Zombie Match. I think we should pause development of the playable for a month or so to make sure we aren't building something that doesn't align with the game's ultimate aesthetic or core game play. Does that work on your end?
Hi <@EMPLOYEE_0008_SLACK_ID>, of course! We’re planning the new start date for the game on November 3rd.
